questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

As it has been raining heavily / since two hours, / the children are / at home.

options.text: As it has been raining heavily

questions.solution:
The erroneous part is 'since two hours,'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect. 
 
• Here, 'for two hours' should be used instead of 'since two hours'.
 
• We use 'for' with a period of time in the past, present, or future.
 
• We use 'since' with a point in time in the past.
 
• *Example: *
 
 
• *He lived in Oxford for 3 years and then he moved. (completed past)*
 
• *They’ve lived in Oxford since 2004.*
 
 
 
• In the given sentence 'two hours' is a period of time hence 'for' will be used.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Correct Sentence:__ *As it has been raining heavily for two hours, the children are at home.*

questions.solution:

__
 
• The underlined part in the given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here,** 'so friendly as'** should be used instead of **'so friendly like'.**
 
• We often use so when we mean ‘to such a great extent’.
 
• With this meaning, '**so**' is** a degree adverb **that modifies adjectives and other adverbs.

• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

questions.question:
**Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.**

We **__might as well__** watch a film on TV as there’s nothing much to do.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'No improvement required'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically correct.
 
• We know that after the **modal verb** **the base form **of the **verb** is used.
 
• Here, '**watch**' is used which is in the **base form.**
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

**Correct Sentence:__** *We **might as well **watch a film on TV as there's nothing much to do.* 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• In the given question, "as well" is an adverbial phrase that is written in-between the auxiliary verb and the main verb. In the sentence, it means "also". Hence, the improvement is not required in the given sentence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

We use **might as well **or **may as well **to suggest doing something because there is nothing better to do or because it has some advantage. For example:

 
• We might as well watch a film on TV as there’s nothing much to do. (There is no better alternative than watching a film on TV.)
 
• You may as well tell me the truth. I’ll find out anyway. (It is better for you to tell me the truth.)

The other options are incorrect and do not make sense in the sentence.

questions.question:
**Select the correct active voice form of the given sentence.**

All the inmates were rescued from the building by the firemen.

options.text: The firemen are rescuing all the inmates from the building.
The firemen have been rescuing all the inmates from the building.
The firemen have rescued all the inmates from the building.
The firemen rescued all the inmates from the building.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**The firemen rescued all the inmates from the building.**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The given sentence is in Passive Voice. As per the given question, we have to change it into Active Voice. 
 
• The structure of the given sentence is as follows:
 
 
• Subject + V₂ + Object. (Active Voice)
 
• Subject (objective case) + was/were + V₃ + Object (subjective case). (Passive Voice)
 
 
 
• *Example:*
 
 
• *Their cousin showed them some rare photographs. (Active Voice)*
 
• *They were shown some rare photographs by their cousin. (Passive Voice)*
 
 
 
• The subject of the given sentence is 'All the inmates'.​​
 
• The object of the given sentence is 'the firemen'. 
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject.
 
• And 'were rescued' will be changed into 'rescued'. 
 
• Lastly, the preposition 'by' will be removed. 

 

Correct Sentence:__ *The firemen rescued all the inmates from the building.*

questions.question:
**Given below are four sentences which are jumbled. Pick the option that gives their correct order.**

A. Schools are closed for the Christmas and winter break at this time of the year.

B. Christmas and New Year are the time of the year to celebrate.

C. All over the city, winter carnivals and Christmas bazaars lend fun and warmth in the cold.

D. For the second time in a row, we are likely to see restrained celebrations for fear of the pandemic raising its ugly head again.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**BACD**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given question is an example of a Para Jumble.
 
• We know that the first statement of a para jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, starting of an incident, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'.
 
• **Sentence B** will be the first sentence because it is an introductory sentence that tells us about Christmas and New Year.
 
• **Sentence A** will be the next sentence because it further tells us that schools are closed during this time.
 
• **Sentence C** will be the next sentence because it tells us that winter carnivals and Christmas bazaars can be seen during this time.
 
• Lastly, **Sentence D** will be used.
 
• Thus, the correct sequence is:
 
 
• **B**: Christmas and New Year are the time of the year to celebrate.
 
• **A**: Schools are closed for the Christmas and winter break at this time of the year.
 
• **C**: All over the city, winter carnivals and Christmas bazaars lend fun and warmth in the cold.
 
• **D**: For the second time in a row, we are likely to see restrained celebrations for fear of the pandemic raising its ugly head again.

 
 
 

**Correct Sequence:__** ***(B).** Christmas and New Year are the time of the year to celebrate.** (A).** Schools are closed for the Christmas and winter break at this time of the year. **(C). **All over the city, winter carnivals and Christmas bazaars lend fun and warmth in the cold. **(D).** For the second time in a row, we are likely to see restrained celebrations for fear of the pandemic raising its ugly head again.*

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

The teacher said, “Asif, go and wash your hands.”

options.text: The teacher told Asif go and wash your hands.
The teacher told Asif go and wash his hands.
The teacher told to Asif to go and wash his hands.
The teacher told Asif to go and wash his hands.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'The teacher told Asif to go and wash his hands.'**

***__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in Direct Speech. As per the question we have to change it into Indirect Speech. 
 
• The process of transformation is as follows:
 
 
• The given sentence is an example of an imperative sentence.
 
• Let's look at the rules of transformation:
 
• While changing the narration of an **imperative sentence**, we need to follow the given steps:
 
 
• The notion of the given sentence is '**suggestion**'.
 
• The conjunction '**to**' should be used in place of** a comma **(,) and** inverted commas **(“ ”). '**said**' will be changed into '**told**'.
 
• '**to**' is followed by '**V₁**'.
 
• '**your**' will be changed into '**his**' because **second-person pronouns** are changed according to the **object** of the **reporting verb.**
 
• *Example:*
 
 
• *The queen said to his servant, "Cook me some delicious food today." (Direct Speech)*
 
• *The queen ordered his servant to cook her some delicious food that day. (Indirect Speech)*

 
 
 
 
 
 
 

Correct Sentence:__ The teacher told Asif to go and wash his hands.*
